purpose: Second benchmark for the attack-family turnover analysis: chronological periods whose attack families are absent from training, with a held-out seen-family control.

cal.rule: flow START at/after start and END before end

period_a.rule: flow START at/after start and END before end

period_b.rule: flow START at/after start and END before end

clients.assignment: client index = splitmix64(row_id XOR 20261127) mod 6, label-free and time-free. Endpoint clients are not used because every training attack targets one server (172.31.69.25), so endpoint clients would place all training attacks on one client.
clients.weights: private training population share per client

sampling.algorithm: smallest splitmix64(row_id XOR 20261126) per cell; label-free
sampling.seen: held-out seen-family control: training-window rows not selected into the training sample, ranked by splitmix64(row_id XOR 20261129); evaluated against the 1% FPR threshold of its own benign rows
sampling.weight: eligible cell rows / sampled cell rows

features: identical to the NF-ToN-IoT-v3 preparer: drop FLOW_START_MILLISECONDS, FLOW_END_MILLISECONDS, IPV4_SRC_ADDR, IPV4_DST_ADDR, L4_SRC_PORT, DNS_QUERY_ID, Label, Attack; categorical PROTOCOL and L7_PROTO one-hot with training vocabulary plus UNKNOWN; remaining numeric log1p, training-sample mean/std, clip [-8,8], float32

root.selection: uniform without replacement from sampled training rows per client, labels not used

training: cross_testbed_runner_v1.py and protocol cross-testbed-adaptive-v1 unchanged except seeds [29, 43]
analysis: same as NF-ToN-IoT-v3 matched panel: oracle recall and AUC at 1% FPR per period, materiality 1 pp, paired bootstrap, pool exchange, family decomposition with Bot share, mix-stability profile, seen-family control, historical-threshold FPR
